proofs.proof_tex:
Put
\[
U_k=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}c_{kq}e_q .
\]
All sums are finite.  Assumption \(\texttt{ass:centered-errors}\) gives
\(E_{P_n}U_k=0\).  Hence, for \(k,k'\in\mathcal K_n\), bilinearity of
covariance gives
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_{P_n}(U_k,U_{k'})
=\sum_{q,q'\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}
  c_{kq}c_{k'q'}E_{P_n}[e_qe_{q'}].
\]
If \(q\ne q'\), assumption \(\texttt{ass:independent-cells}\) and
centeredness imply
\[
E_{P_n}[e_qe_{q'}]=E_{P_n}[e_q]E_{P_n}[e_{q'}]=0.
\]
For \(q=q'=(u,v)\), the definition of \(\sigma_{uv}^2\) gives
\(E_{P_n}[e_q^2]=\sigma_{uv}^2=\sigma_q^2\).  Therefore
\[
\operatorname{Cov}_{P_n}(U_k,U_{k'})
=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}c_{kq}c_{k'q}\sigma_q^2
=\Omega_{kk'},
\]
where the last equality is the definition of \(\Omega_n\).  By the
definition of \(\mathcal Q_{n,kk'}^{\mathrm{sh}}\), every omitted summand
has \(c_{kq}c_{k'q}=0\), so
\[
\Omega_{kk'}
=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_{n,kk'}^{\mathrm{sh}}}
  c_{kq}c_{k'q}\sigma_q^2.
\]
This equality also proves the asserted nonzero characterization: its
left-hand side is nonzero if and only if the displayed signed sum is
nonzero.  No termwise noncancellation is asserted.  Finally, assumption
\(\texttt{ass:horizon-variance-nondegeneracy}\) gives \(s_k>0\) for every
\(k\), so \(D_n\) is invertible.  The definition of \(\Sigma_n\) then
gives \(\Sigma_n=D_n^{-1}\Omega_nD_n^{-1}\).

In \(\mathcal W^{(2)}\),
\[
M^0=\mathbf 1_8\mathbf 1_3^{\top},
\]
so \(\operatorname{rank}(M^0)=1\).  For either \(k\in\{0,1\}\), the
eligible Choi--Yuan block is the \(8\)-by-\(2\) all-ones matrix.  One
compact singular value decomposition has
\[
U_{2,k}=\frac{\mathbf 1_8}{\sqrt 8},\qquad
V_{2,k}=\frac{\mathbf 1_2}{\sqrt 2},\qquad
\psi_{2,k}=\sqrt{8\cdot2}=4.
\]
Consequently
\[
\mu_{2,k}
=\max\left\{8\left\|U_{2,k}\right\|_{2,\infty}^2,
2\left\|V_{2,k}\right\|_{2,\infty}^2\right\}
=\max\{8(1/8),2(1/2)\}=1.
\]
Because every loading and factor equals one and the donor and pre-period
sets have cardinalities four and one, respectively,
\[
A_{2,k}=\sum_{j=5}^8x_j^2=4,
\qquad
B_2=\sum_{s\in S_2}z_s^2=z_1^2=1.
\]
For both horizons, \(E_k=\{2\}\), \(N_k=n_2=4\), and hence the outer
cohort weight in the definition of \(c_{kq}\) is one.  Substitution into
that definition gives, with \(t_k=2+k\),
\[
c_{k,(u,v)}=
\begin{cases}
  1/4,&u\in I_2,\ v=t_k,\\
 -1/4,&u\in J_{2,k},\ v=t_k,\\
 -1/4,&u\in I_2,\ v=1,\\
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
The three nonzero cases are disjoint and each contains four cells.
Since every cell variance is one, the definition of \(\Omega_n\) yields
\[
\Omega_{kk}=4(1/4)^2+4(-1/4)^2+4(-1/4)^2=\frac34.
\]
The treated target cells and donor target cells occur at calendar time
\(2+k\), and therefore are distinct across \(k=0\) and \(k=1\).  The
only shared nonzero cells are the four cells \((u,1)\) with \(u\in I_2\).
Each contributes
\[
c_{0,(u,1)}c_{1,(u,1)}=(-1/4)(-1/4)=\frac1{16}.
\]
Applying \(\texttt{lem:staircase-covariance}\) therefore gives
\[
\Omega_{01}=4\left(\frac1{16}\right)=\frac14,
\qquad
\Sigma_{01}=\frac{\Omega_{01}}{
\sqrt{\Omega_{00}\Omega_{11}}}
=\frac{1/4}{3/4}=\frac13.
\]
Thus the signed shared-cell sum is nonzero, as claimed.

Under the proposed positivity qualification, let \(E_0=\{g_0\}\).
Then \(N_0=n_{g_0}\), so the outer weight \(n_{g_0}/N_0\) in the
definition of \(c_{0q}\) equals one.  The displayed formula for
\(c_{0,(u,v)}\) consequently becomes
\[
\frac{\mathbf 1\{u\in I_{g_0},\ v=g_0\}}{n_{g_0}}
-\mathbf 1\{u\in J_{g_0,0},\ v=g_0\}
 \bar x_{g_0}^{\top}A_{g_0,0}^{-1}x_u
-\frac{\mathbf 1\{u\in I_{g_0},\ v\in S_{g_0}\}}{n_{g_0}}
 z_{g_0}^{\top}B_{g_0}^{-1}z_v,
\]
which is exactly the single-block coefficient to which
\(\texttt{def:staircase-influence-map}\) refers.  With only one
coordinate, the covariance and its feasible counterpart are, directly
from their definitions,
\[
\Omega_{00}=\sum_{q=(u,v)\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}
c_{0q}^2\sigma_{uv}^2,
\qquad
\widehat\Omega_{00}=\sum_{q=(u,v)\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}
\widehat c_{0q}^{,2}\widehat\sigma_u^2.
\]
Assumption \(\texttt{ass:row-heteroskedasticity}\), which is a member
property of the class used by the plug-in construction, changes the
first display's variance to \(\sigma_u^2\); the second display is thus
the corresponding unit-residual plug-in form.

It remains to check the scalar critical value.  The proposed condition
\(\widehat\Omega_{00}>0\) implies
\(\widehat s_0=\sqrt{\widehat\Omega_{00}}>0\), so the division in the
multiplier statistic is defined.  Conditional on \(Y\), independence
and normality of the multipliers give
\[
\widetilde Z
=\sum_{q=(u,v)\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}
  \frac{\widehat c_{0q}\widehat\sigma_u}{\widehat s_0}\xi_q
\sim N\!\left(0,
\frac{\sum_q\widehat c_{0q}^{,2}\widehat\sigma_u^2}
     {\widehat s_0^2}\right)
=N(0,1).
\]
Thus \(W_n^\xi=|\widetilde Z|\), its conditional \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile
is the ordinary two-sided standard-normal critical value, and
\(\mathcal C_{n,0}=[\widehat\tau_0\pm
c_{1-\alpha,n}\widehat s_0]\) is the ordinary studentized scalar
interval.  Every reduction is algebraic; no growing-dimensional limit
theorem is used.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: When \(K=1\), \(\mathcal K_n=\{0\}\), the eligible set contains one target block \(E_0=\{g_0\}\), and \(\widehat\Omega_{00}>0\), \(c_{0q}\) and \(\Omega_{00}\) reduce to the Choi--Yuan Proposition A.4 influence coefficients and their heteroskedastic scalar influence variance, while \(\widehat\Omega_{00}\) and \(\mathcal C_{n,0}\) reduce to the Choi--Kwon--Liao-style unit-residual plug-in variance and the ordinary studentized scalar interval.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The multiplier statistic divides by \(\widehat s_0=\sqrt{\widehat\Omega_{00}}\).  The frozen core assumes positivity of the population scale only, so the exact finite-sample reduction requires \(\widehat\Omega_{00}>0\); without it the displayed multiplier statistic is undefined.

proposed.statement: For all \(k,k'\in\mathcal K_n\), mutual independence and centeredness on \(\mathcal Q_n^+\) give the algebraic identity \[\operatorname{Cov}_{P_n}\!\left(\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}c_{kq}e_q,\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}c_{k'q}e_q\right)=\Omega_{kk'}=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_{n,kk'}^{\mathrm{sh}}}c_{kq}c_{k'q}\sigma_q^2.\] Terms outside \(\mathcal Q_{n,kk'}^{\mathrm{sh}}\) vanish by definition, and \(\Omega_{kk'}\ne0\) if and only if the displayed signed shared-cell sum is nonzero; individual products may cancel. Studentization is the identity \(\Sigma_n=D_n^{-1}\Omega_nD_n^{-1}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The studentization identity uses \(D_n^{-1}\); the existing dependency list omitted the frozen assumption that every \(s_k\) is positive.

proposed.statement: When \(K=1\), \(\mathcal K_n=\{0\}\), the eligible set contains one target block \(E_0=\{g_0\}\), and \(\widehat\Omega_{00}>0\), \(c_{0q}\) and \(\Omega_{00}\) reduce to the Choi--Yuan Proposition A.4 influence coefficients and their heteroskedastic scalar influence variance, while \(\widehat\Omega_{00}\) and \(\mathcal C_{n,0}\) reduce to the Choi--Kwon--Liao-style unit-residual plug-in variance and the ordinary studentized scalar interval.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This applies the proposed positivity qualification and removes the unused growing-dimensional band theorem from an algebraic scalar reduction.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A simultaneous Choi--Yuan block expansion whose nonlinear errors obey \( |r_{gk}|\le C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\) for every eligible \( (g,k)\) on one event with probability tending to one uniformly over \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY}}\).
open_obligations.obstruction: The definition of \(\rho_n\) proves the vector equality but not its stochastic rate.  The frozen core contains only a bibliographic description of Proposition A.4, not a declared cited theorem with a growing-block simultaneous probability bound.  Scalar or blockwise \(O_P\) control does not imply control of a maximum over a growing collection.
open_obligations.attempted: Expanded the eligible-unit aggregation before taking maxima and reduced the target rate to one explicit simultaneous block-remainder event.  Checked the relevant frozen bibliography record; it supplies provenance but no theorem statement or tail probability from which the required union can be proved.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The exact vector equality is already forced by the definition of
\(\rho_n\).  Indeed, because
\(a_{kq}=c_{kq}\sigma_q/s_k\),
\[
\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}a_{kq}\frac{e_q}{\sigma_q}
=s_k^{-1}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}c_{kq}e_q,
\]
and rearranging the definition of \(\rho_{n,k}\) gives the asserted
coordinate equality.  To isolate the missing step, let \(r_{gk}\) denote
the nonlinear remainder in the exact debiased expansion for block
\((g,k)\).  Cohort aggregation would give
\[
\rho_{n,k}=s_k^{-1}\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}r_{gk}.
\]
Consequently, on any event on which
\(\lvert r_{gk}\rvert\le C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\) simultaneously for
all eligible \((g,k)\),
\[
\|\rho_n\|_\infty
\le C\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}s_k^{-1}
\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}
=C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K).
\]
Thus the desired rate follows from, and is reduced exactly to, a
simultaneous block-remainder event with probability tending to one
uniformly over the finite slices.  No such event is a frozen assumption
or established statement.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A primitive uniform rate for the joint estimation error of the feasible event-by-cell score loadings, including both \(\widehat c_{kq}-c_{kq}\) and the leave-one-cell-out unit-variance errors.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen replication condition controls only the number of untreated variance-training cells.  No assumption or established result bounds the leave-one-cell-out imputation error or the estimated Choi--Yuan loading coefficients in the normalized rowwise \(\ell_2\) norm at the required \(o_P((\log(2K))^{-2})\) rate.  Assuming that score-loading rate would assume the theorem's substantive crux.
open_obligations.attempted: Decomposed the normalized covariance error into two score-loading errors and derived a sharp deterministic Cauchy--Schwarz bound.  Tried to obtain the missing rate from variance replication and the unscaled signal, spectral, and block envelopes, but those premises contain no result transporting their rates to \(\widehat c\) or cross-fitted residuals with the required powers of \(\log(2K)\).
open_obligations.partial_result:
The missing stochastic assertion can be isolated by a deterministic
calculation.  Under row heteroskedasticity define
\[
\widehat b_{kq}
=\frac{\widehat c_{kq}\widehat\sigma_u}{s_k},
\qquad
a_{kq}=\frac{c_{kq}\sigma_u}{s_k},
\qquad q=(u,v),
\]
and put
\[
r_n^{\mathrm{score}}
=\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}
\left(\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}
(\widehat b_{kq}-a_{kq})^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
The definition of \(s_k\) gives \(\sum_q a_{kq}^2=1\).  Therefore,
by adding and subtracting the two cross terms and applying
Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{|\widehat\Omega_{kk'}-\Omega_{kk'}|}{s_ks_{k'}}
&=\left|\sum_q\widehat b_{kq}\widehat b_{k'q}
-\sum_q a_{kq}a_{k'q}\right|\\
&\le
\|\widehat b_k-a_k\|_2\|a_{k'}\|_2
+\|a_k\|_2\|\widehat b_{k'}-a_{k'}\|_2
+\|\widehat b_k-a_k\|_2
 \|\widehat b_{k'}-a_{k'}\|_2\\
&\le 2r_n^{\mathrm{score}}+(r_n^{\mathrm{score}})^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Hence the first claimed covariance rate would follow from the primitive
score-loading conclusion
\(r_n^{\mathrm{score}}=o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2})\), uniformly over the
slice.  The diagonal case and
\(\lvert\sqrt{1+x}-1\rvert\le\lvert x\rvert\) for \(x>-1\) then give
the stated standard-error rate (in fact the stronger
\(o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2})\) rate), and division by the two consistently
estimated diagonal scales gives
\(\|\widehat\Sigma_n-\Sigma_n\|_{\max}
=o_{P_n}((\log(2K))^{-2})\).
The frozen assumptions do not establish the displayed
\(\ell_2\)-score-loading conclusion: variance replication controls the
sampling fluctuation of true residual squares, but no frozen result
controls the leave-one-cell-out imputation errors and estimated
Choi--Yuan loading coefficients at this logarithmic rate.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The feasible transfer from the oracle high-dimensional influence sum to the studentized conditional multiplier statistic uniformly over the finite slices.
open_obligations.obstruction: The transfer requires the unresolved uniform influence remainder and feasible covariance rates.  It also requires a theorem-granularity cited Gaussian approximation and anti-concentration result; the frozen bibliography record alone is not a logical premise.  Consequently the claimed coverage cannot be proved without laundering those missing inputs.
open_obligations.attempted: Reduced the oracle statistic to a maximum of independent centered sub-Gaussian vectors with unit marginal variances and coefficient envelope \(L_n(K)\), and wrote the exact perturbation bound showing where \(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\) enters.  The argument closes conditionally on the two unresolved upstream rates but not from the current core.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Let
\[
S_{n,k}=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}
a_{kq}e_q/\sigma_q.
\]
The frozen centeredness and independence assumptions make the vectors
\((a_{kq}e_q/\sigma_q)_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\), indexed by \(q\),
independent and centered, while the definition of \(s_k\) gives
\(\operatorname{Var}_{P_n}(S_{n,k})=1\).  The sub-Gaussian assumption
and the cell-leverage condition are the inputs for a published
high-dimensional Gaussian approximation after replacing the absolute
maximum by a maximum in dimension \(2K\).  If that cited approximation
is materialized, the standard perturbation inequality is
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\sup_z\left|
P_n\{\max_k|S_{n,k}+\rho_{n,k}|\le z\}
-P_n\{\max_k|Z_{n,k}|\le z\}\right|\\
&\quad\le
\text{Gaussian-approximation error}
+P_n\{\|\rho_n\|_\infty>d_n\}
+\sup_zP\{z-d_n<\max_k|Z_{n,k}|\le z+d_n\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Gaussian anti-concentration bounds the last term by a constant times
\(d_n\sqrt{\log(2K)}\).  Thus the frozen remainder envelope would make
this term vanish if the missing uniform influence bound held.  The
deterministic covariance comparison in the preceding partial result
would then transfer the oracle Gaussian law to the feasible conditional
multiplier law and the estimated standard errors.  At present both of
those load-bearing inputs are open, so the asserted feasible coverage
conclusion cannot be derived from the frozen core.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The exact second-order Choi--Yuan remainder on a legal balanced rank-one triangular array and a matching lower bound for its \(1-\eta_n\) quantile with signs aligned across horizons.
open_obligations.obstruction: The published envelope \(R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\) is only an upper perturbation expression.  The frozen definition of \(\widehat M^0\) names the estimator but omits its objective, tuning parameters, KKT equations, and debiasing formula, so the mandated early-kill second-order calculation is not determined by the available primitives.  The two-horizon witness certifies linear covariance only and supplies no nonlinear-remainder lower bound.
open_obligations.attempted: First tested whether the rank-one witness could yield an attained remainder from the displayed influence coefficients.  Those coefficients determine only the first-order term; every second-order term depends on the unspecified estimator map.  Also compared the exact modulus definition with \(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\): a simultaneous block tail bound would prove only the upper inequality, while successive norm inequalities provide no reverse inequality or undercoverage sign.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The definitions do identify the exact, but nonprimitive, frontier:
\[
\Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)
=\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}
\inf\{d\ge0:P_n(\|\rho_n\|_\infty>d)\le\eta_n\}.
\]
If a simultaneous block event of the form isolated in the uniform
influence partial result were available with tail probability at most
\(\eta_n\), it would imply the computable one-sided bound
\[
\Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)\le C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K).
\]
This is only an upper bound.  Each term in
\(R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\) results from norm inequalities, and neither an
upper perturbation bound nor the linear two-horizon covariance witness
implies that any legal low-rank panel attains one of those terms with an
aligned sign.  The frozen construction of \(\widehat M^0\) names the
Choi--Yuan procedure but does not give its objective, tuning parameters,
KKT equations, or debiasing formula.  Therefore its exact second-order
remainder cannot be computed from the frozen primitives, and no lower
bound comparable to a primitive block-ratio expression has been proved.
